claim: Solanezumab improves cognition in Alzheimer's disease
gold_rationale: Every adequately powered phase 3 solanezumab trial with a cognitive primary endpoint was negative, across the full AD severity spectrum. EXPEDITION1 & EXPEDITION2 (Doody, NEJM 2014, N=2052 mild-to-moderate AD) missed the ADAS-cog primary. EXPEDITION3 (Honig, NEJM 2018, NCT01900665, N=2129 mild AD dementia) failed its primary ADAS-cog14 endpoint (difference vs placebo -0.80, 95% CI -1.73 to 0.14, P=0.10), after which Eli Lilly halted development for symptomatic AD. The A4 study (Sperling, NEJM 2023, NCT02008357, N=1169 preclinical AD) showed solanezumab 'did not slow cognitive decline' on the PACC over 240 weeks (difference -0.30, P=0.26). A systematic review/meta-analysis of anti-Aβ agents (Lu, JNNP 2020, 19 RCTs, N=12,903) found no clinically important cognitive benefit (ADAS-cog MD 0.20, 95% CI -0.40 to 0.81, below the 3.1-3.8 minimal important difference). Solanezumab was never approved by the FDA or any regulator for AD (ALZFORUM: FDA status Discontinued, Approved for: None; development ended March 2023). The clinical/regulatory consensus is therefore that solanezumab does not improve cognition in Alzheimer's disease — the claim is Not Supported. (An anti-monomer/soluble-Aβ mechanism distinguishes it from later plaque-clearing antibodies lecanemab/donanemab, which DID slow decline — but that does not rescue the solanezumab-specific claim.)
provenance: PubMed (verified PMIDs + DOIs + publication types), ClinicalTrials.gov (verified NCTs, enrollment, phase, primary endpoints), FDA/regulatory status via ALZFORUM + Eli Lilly press release (Exa). All primary cognitive endpoints, effect sizes, and directions read directly from published NEJM/JNNP abstracts.

rows.citation: Honig LS, et al. Trial of Solanezumab for Mild Dementia Due to Alzheimer's Disease (EXPEDITION3). N Engl J Med. 2018;378:321-330. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1705971
rows.integrity_note: Pivotal phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled; NCT01900665 (verified, enrollment 2129, phase 3, terminated); industry-sponsored (Eli Lilly), pre-registered, primary endpoint reported. PubMed pub types include 'Clinical Trial, Phase III' + 'Randomized Controlled Trial'. No integrity concerns; no retraction.
rows.finding: In mild AD dementia (MMSE 20-26, amyloid-positive), solanezumab 400 mg IV q4w did NOT significantly slow decline on the primary ADAS-cog14 endpoint (difference -0.80, 95% CI -1.73 to 0.14, P=0.10). 2129 enrolled (1057 solanezumab, 1072 placebo). Trial failed; Lilly ended symptomatic-AD development.

rows.citation: Doody RS, et al. Phase 3 Trials of Solanezumab for Mild-to-Moderate Alzheimer's Disease (EXPEDITION1 & EXPEDITION2). N Engl J Med. 2014;370:311-321. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1312889
rows.integrity_note: Two parallel pivotal phase 3 RCTs (NCT00905372, NCT00904683); double-blind, placebo-controlled; primary cognitive endpoints pre-specified and reported. PubMed pub types include 'Clinical Trial, Phase III' + 'Randomized Controlled Trial'. No integrity concerns; no retraction. n_int=1012 = total randomized in EXPEDITION1 (506+506); EXPEDITION2 randomized 1040 (521+519), pooled N=2052.
rows.finding: In mild-to-moderate AD, solanezumab 400 mg IV q4w for 18 months did NOT meet the primary ADAS-cog11 cognitive endpoint in either trial (EXPEDITION1 ADAS-cog11 diff -0.8, P=0.24; EXPEDITION2 mild-AD ADAS-cog14 diff -1.5 to -1.7, NS). Both trials negative on the primary cognitive outcome (pooled N=2052).

rows.citation: Sperling RA, et al. Trial of Solanezumab in Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease (A4 Study). N Engl J Med. 2023;389:1096-1107. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2305032
rows.integrity_note: Phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled early-intervention trial; NCT02008357 (verified, enrollment 1169, phase 3, PACC primary over 240 wks); NIA-funded. PubMed pub type 'Randomized Controlled Trial'. No integrity concerns; no retraction. n_int corrected from 585 to 578 per NEJM abstract (578 solanezumab, 591 placebo, 1169 total).
rows.finding: In preclinical AD (CDR 0, MMSE>=25, amyloid-positive), solanezumab (up to 1600 mg IV q4w) 'did not slow cognitive decline as compared with placebo over 240 weeks' on the primary PACC (mean change -1.43 solanezumab vs -1.13 placebo; difference -0.30, 95% CI -0.82 to 0.22, P=0.26). 1169 randomized (578 solanezumab, 591 placebo). Negative even at the earliest disease stage; ended solanezumab development.

rows.citation: Lu L, et al. Anti-Aβ agents for mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease: systematic review and meta-analysis. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 2020;91:1316-1324. DOI:10.1136/jnnp-2020-323497
rows.integrity_note: Systematic review/meta-analysis; 19 RCTs, 17 at low risk of bias; random-effects pooling; includes solanezumab among anti-Aβ agents. PubMed pub types 'Meta-Analysis' + 'Systematic Review'. No integrity concerns; no retraction.
rows.finding: Across 19 RCTs of anti-Aβ agents (N=12,903), no cognitive difference vs placebo on ADAS-Cog (MD 0.20, 95% CI -0.40 to 0.81; below the 3.1-3.8-point minimal important difference; moderate-certainty evidence). Authors conclude anti-Aβ interventions are unlikely to meaningfully slow cognitive/functional decline — situating solanezumab's failures in the broader negative evidence base. (n_int is total analyzed N across arms, not solanezumab-only.)

baseline.text: Solanezumab has failed to demonstrate meaningful cognitive benefit in Alzheimer's disease across multiple large clinical trials.

notes: All four rows re-verified against PubMed metadata (title/journal/DOI/pub-types/year/first-author) and, where applicable, ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT, enrollment, phase, primary endpoint). Effect sizes and directions read directly from primary NEJM/JNNP abstracts and all match the corpus. One numeric correction applied: A4 solanezumab n_int 585 -> 578. No retracted publications found in the solanezumab efficacy literature. FDA non-approval / March-2023 discontinuation confirmed via ALZFORUM + Eli Lilly release. DIAN-TU (NCT01760005) solanezumab arm also negative but not used as a core row (complex platform design); the four included rows span mild-to-moderate, mild, preclinical, and pooled evidence. build_confidence high — one of the clearest 'Not Supported' cases in the AD anti-amyloid literature.
